newsitem.title: UK: Precious outlook - Gold vulnerable to more losses.
newsitem.headline: Precious outlook - Gold vulnerable to more losses.

text.p: Gold's tumble below a key resistance level last week suggests further losses are looming this week, with $370 an eventual objective, analysts said.
Bullion ended last week in London at $376.90/$377.40 an ounce, more than $3 lower than it started, after tenacious support around $377 crumpled on Thursday afternoon.
Gold was still lower early on Monday, threatening to break below interim support at $375.
The sell-off, attributed to protracted heavy selling by speculative investment funds and producers, sent spot prices briefly below $376.
The next significant price move is likely to be still lower, analysts and dealers said.
"Gold had been trampolining between $377-$377.50 and $384-$385 for a time. I think we've resolved that with fresh breaks to the downside," said Cliff Green of Trend Analysis.
The breach of support left gold oversold and a period of consolidation was likely, with possible short-term corrections to around $379, analysts said.
The market was also concentrating on the expiry of over-the-counter options on Wednesday, and dealers felt uncomfortable taking large positions ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
But eventually gold was likely to test the historically significant $370 support level, which represented the bottom of a broad trading range going back to 1994, analysts said.
"I'm bearish and looking for a test of that low. Rallies will be corrective, short lived and insubstantial," Green said.
Merrill Lynch metals analyst Ted Arnold also pegged gold to head lower, putting its trading range over the next two months at between $360 and $390 in his latest monthly report.
"Gold is continuing to erode away in a very slow but steady fashion with most bullion dealers looking for $370 basis spot as the downside target before the end of the year," Arnold said.
On the way down, support was expected to emerge at $375 and $373, although bulls were hoping for a reversal in the downtrend if gold could claw above previous support.
So far, dealers said gold was finding just minimal support from physical buying even at the new lower levels and despite the traditional seasonal peak in demand.
The World Gold Council reported last week that demand year-to-date was down four percent at 1,566 tonnes compared with last year.

Concerns about possible gold sales by European central banks and the International Monetary Fund continued to spook the market, as did the prospect of under-hedged producers flooding the market with forward sales by the end of the year. Silver was also trending lower, but managed to hold within recent ranges, starting the week around $4.83/$4.85 an ounce.
Green said, "I'm quite bearish for silver, with the short-term objective at $4.60 and then the $4.35-$4.40 area. That's where longer- term support will be coming in."
